text: She weaves by that open door. Her shuttle stall. The night grew still. No sound aloom, just breath and will.  The scroll came down. She softly cried. Father's name right inside. No brother, no elder son. I'll ride for him. The time has come. She bought a steed, her reigns, her sword. My daughter's love a warrior's word. No kiss goodbye, no parting please. She rides beneath the breaking dawn. At dust she camps where rivers brea to hear her journey draw. Through mountain dark and

Barren land. She bore the storm she faced the snow. Iron rang and war did grow. Peace returned and glory shown. She asked for none just to go home. The concept come take gold and see about stood aside. Just let me feel my village street. My mother's arms my father's pride. A thousand miles her camel ran back to where life began. Her mama wept. Her sister danced. Her boots stepped down the wor. She loosed her hair. She dropped her blade and peace upon her soul was laid. Her comrades came with mouths a gay 12 years and never once they knew. The rabbits sleep through dusk and shade.

Can't tell which from who is who. It ain't the form we wear that shif from deep inside. Ride on the moon landing. Ride strong moving through storm and steel and morning song. Ride on moon land. Brave soul move and the Lord walks with the ones who carry on.  Amen. She carried it on.  Oh yes, she carried on.
